p.head: Project Structure
p.p: Each project in the Jewish Liturgy TEI schema must contain a TEI document called index.xml that serves as the main entry point for the project. This file must include:
The index.xml file serves as the central organizing document for the project, linking to other TEI documents through ptr or ref elements as needed.

p.head: Biblical Texts
p.p: Biblical texts in this schema follow these structural and markup conventions:

list.item: The primary structural unit is the paragraph (tei:p)

Paragraphs are typed using the type attribute with values:
open-N: Paragraph starts with N open parashah markers (פתוחות)
closed-N: Paragraph starts with N closed parashah markers (סתומות)
Where N is a number indicating the quantity of markers
Chapters are marked with milestone element with unit="chapter" and n indicating the chapter number
Verses are marked with milestone element with unit="verse" and n indicating the verse number
When both Kri (read) and Ktiv (written) forms exist, they are marked up as: <choice> <j:read>...</j:read> <j:written>...</j:written> </choice>
When only Kri or only Ktiv form exists, the choice element is optional
Kri text is always wrapped in j:read
Ktiv text is always wrapped in j:written

moduleSpec.desc: Custom elements for the Open Siddur Jewish Liturgy Project TEI schema

moduleRef.include: ab anchor link seg standOff linkGrp

elementSpec.desc: An element that includes content from another part of the document.

attDef.desc: Specifies the path of the target to be included.
Specifies where the transclusion should end (inclusive). If not provided, anything enclosed by target will be transcluded.
Specifies the type of transclusion to perform. If no type is specified, the default is external.

valItem.desc: Include both XML hierarchy and text content.
Include only text content, without XML hierarchy.

constraintSpec.desc: Schematron rule ensuring targetEnd names a single point, not a range: a transclusion spanning a range is written as target alone (itself possibly a range) or target/targetEnd naming two points, never as a ranged targetEnd.

sch:assert.test: not(@targetEnd) or not(starts-with(@targetEnd, 'urn:x-opensiddur:')) or not(some $t in tokenize(@targetEnd, '/')[position() gt 1] satisfies contains($t, '-'))

sch:rule.sch:assert: targetEnd must not itself be a ranged URN; split this into two transclude elements instead.

attDef.desc: Characterizes the element in some sense, using any convenient classification scheme or typology.

elementSpec.desc: Indicates that the enclosed text is a divine name (e.g., the Tetragrammaton or other epithet) for special handling by downstream processors.

Contains the text as it is read (kri) when it differs from the written form (ktiv). Used in Hebrew text to represent the traditional pronunciation of words that are written differently in the text. Typically appears within a <choice> element alongside a <written> element.

Contains the text as it is written (ktiv) when it differs from the read form (kri). Used in Hebrew text to represent the written form of words that are pronounced differently. Typically appears within a <choice> element alongside a <read> element.

One of several alternate wordings of the same text, exactly one of which is read. Appears within a <choice> element alongside one or more other <option> elements. Use xml:lang when the options differ in language, and corresp to carry a URN by which a setting may select an option. Contrast conditional, which governs text that is either said or omitted.

constraintSpec.desc: Schematron rules to ensure option is used as a set of mutually exclusive alternates, and is not mixed with the kri/ktiv vocabulary.

sch:rule.sch:assert: A choice containing option must contain at least two of them: an alternate is a choice between readings.
option must not appear beside read or written: alternate wordings and kri/ktiv pairs are different things.

elementSpec.desc: Associates a set of conditional attribute declarations with a range of text. Used to specify that the following content is to be processed with the given declarations in effect, until the corresponding endDeclare element, which is required. Contains one or more feature structures representing the declarations, each with a type and at least one feature, and nothing else. A declaration gives values, never alternatives: vAlt and vNot belong in conditions.

Marks the end of the scope of a set of conditional attribute declarations previously established by a set element. The endDeclare element must have a required target attribute, which points to the xml:id of the corresponding declare element in the same file.

attDef.desc: Points to the xml:id of the declare element whose settings declarations are being ended. The value must be a URI reference (typically a fragment identifier, e.g., "#setting1") that refers to a declare element in the same file.

constraintSpec.desc: Schematron rules to ensure that the target attribute of undeclare points to a declare element in the same file.

sch:rule.sch:assert: Every declare element must have an xml:id attribute.

Every declare element must be closed by an endDeclare element that follows it and names it in its target attribute. A declaration that is never closed governs the rest of the file, and leaks into whatever transcludes it.
A declare element holds only feature structures (tei:fs).
A declaration gives values, not alternatives: tei:vAlt and tei:vNot belong in conditions.
The endDeclare element must have a target attribute.
The target attribute must be a fragment identifier (start with '#').
The target attribute must point to a declare element in the same file.
The targeted declare element must precede the endDeclare element in document order.

A declaration's scope must fully contain every element that begins inside it. An element that begins after the declare and still holds the endDeclare may be left out -- by a false condition or a transcluded range -- and the marker that ends the declaration goes with it.

A declare and its endDeclare must be siblings. A declaration that begins inside an element and ends outside it is pushed only when that element is processed; when it is left out, the endDeclare ends a declaration that was never made.

elementSpec.desc: Declares a conditional scope for settings or features. The conditional element may contain a single tei:note (for documentation or explanation), followed by one or more feature value structures (members of ).

attDef.desc: How the source sets the passage off when the condition cannot be decided. Without it, an undecided scope is set off by its instruction tei:note if it has one, and otherwise not at all: a conditional with neither is a direction to the processor, not to the reader.

valItem.desc: The source itself marks the passage off, with brackets, parentheses or a line, so the standard delimiters are reproduced around it.

constraintSpec.desc: Schematron rule to ensure a conditional can be closed by an endConditional, which references it by xml:id.

sch:rule.sch:assert: Every conditional element must have an xml:id attribute.

Every conditional element must be closed by an endConditional element that follows it and names it in its target attribute. A conditional that is never closed governs the rest of the file, which is almost never what was meant and is otherwise not reported.

The note of a conditional is the rubric saying when its passage is said, an instruction (type="instruction"). A rubric saying what the passage is, a description (type="description"), goes inside the scope.

constraintSpec.desc: A feature structure in a condition or a declaration names its type and holds at least one feature: the type is what the features are features of, and a structure with none says nothing.

sch:rule.sch:assert: A feature structure in a condition or a declaration must have a type attribute.
A feature structure in a condition or a declaration must hold at least one feature.

elementSpec.desc: A condition on whether the standoff tei:note that contains it is printed at all. It is evaluated against the settings in scope where the note would be inserted: if it is false, the note (and its reference mark) is omitted; if it is true or undefined, the note is printed. Unlike conditional, it opens no scope and has no end marker. Conditioning part of a note's text is done with conditional inside the note.

constraintSpec.desc: A condition is the first child of a standoff note that is not an instruction.

sch:rule.sch:assert: A condition must be the first child of a tei:note.
A condition applies to notes in a notes standOff; text is conditioned with conditional.
Instructions and descriptions are conditioned with conditional, not condition.

elementSpec.desc: Marks the end of the scope of a conditional element. The endConditional element must have a required target attribute, which points to the xml:id of the corresponding conditional element in the same file.

attDef.desc: Points to the xml:id of the conditional element whose scope is being ended. The value must be a URI reference (typically a fragment identifier, e.g., "#cond1") that refers to a conditional element in the same file.

constraintSpec.desc: Schematron rules to ensure that the target attribute of endConditional points to a conditional element in the same file and that the referenced element precedes the endConditional element.

sch:rule.sch:assert: The endConditional element must have a target attribute.
The target attribute must be a fragment identifier (start with '#').
The target attribute must point to a conditional element in the same file.
The referenced conditional element must precede the endConditional element.

A conditional scope must fully contain every element that begins inside it. An element that begins after the conditional and still holds the endConditional is only partly governed by the scope -- and when the condition resolves false, that element is discarded along with the marker that ends the scope, so the scope never closes and governs the rest of the file. Put the markers outside the hierarchy they cross.

elementSpec.desc: Evaluates to true only if all contained feature value structures evaluate to true with respect to the currently in scope declared settings.
Evaluates to true if any one of the contained feature value structures evaluates to true with respect to the currently in scope declared settings.
Evaluates to true only if none of the contained feature value structures evaluates to true with respect to the currently in scope declared settings.
Evaluates to true only if exactly one of the contained feature value structures evaluates to true with respect to the currently in scope declared settings.

constraintSpec.desc: Global validation rules that apply to all attributes in the document.

sch:rule.sch:assert: The TEI element must declare a default language using the xml:lang attribute.
Attribute must not be empty or contain only whitespace.

constraintSpec.desc:
A text URN names one stretch of text, so it may appear on at most one element per document. A repeated corresp breaks alignment and resolution silently: the reference database keeps only the first element bearing it, and the parallel compiler drops every segment after the first.
Only text URNs are identities. A condition URN is a feature *name* and is meant to repeat — one setting selects the ta'am elyon reading everywhere it occurs — so it is deliberately outside this rule.

sch:rule.sch:report: The corresp is used more than once in this document. Each text URN must identify exactly one element.

constraintSpec.desc:
A contributor URN on @ref names a person, and nothing downstream can tell a misspelt identifier from a second contributor: the credit simply appears under a name nobody has. So the shape is checked here, where every validation sees it, rather than only at typeset time.
Grammar only. Whether the identifier names anyone we know is a roster question, and the registry in specs/urn_registry/ answers it -- Schematron cannot read that file. Keep the namespace list in step with CONTRIBUTOR_NAMESPACES in opensiddur/common/urn_registry.py.

sch:rule.sch:assert: The @ref is not a contributor URN. It must read urn:x-opensiddur:contributor:<namespace>/<identifier>, where the namespace is en.wikisource.org, he.wikisource.org or opensiddur.org.

constraintSpec.desc: An edition-verse milestone records an edition's own numbering, not an identity.

sch:rule.sch:assert: A milestone with unit="edition-verse" must carry the edition's verse number in @n.
A milestone with unit="edition-verse" must not carry @corresp: it records an edition's own numbering for display, and only the canonical unit="verse" milestone identifies the text.

constraintSpec.desc: The two sub-verse units divide a verse and hang their URN one component below it.

sch:rule.sch:assert: A milestone with unit="half-verse" must carry @n of "a" or "b": a verse has a first half and a second, divided at the etnachta.
A numbered half-verse must carry @corresp. A bare half-verse milestone with neither @n nor @corresp is a terminator and opens no scope.
A half-verse's @corresp must be the verse's URN with "/a" or "/b" after it, matching @n.
A named verse-part must carry @corresp. A bare verse-part milestone with neither @n nor @corresp is a terminator and opens no scope.
A verse part's name may not contain "-": a dash in the last component of a URN is what marks a range. Transliterations use "_".
"a" and "b" are reserved for the accentual halves; a verse part must be named for the word it begins on.
